indicators.note: taking means the word for stop holds the drug's letter within it

parts.note: to stop doing something is to quit
E is the street abbreviation for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Advice to someone to give up the drug ecstasy, even now.
explanation.definitionFit: Still and quiet are synonyms describing calm, silent conditions.

parts.note: read as 'something watering can (do), possibly': the verb for supplying water to land, not the garden vessel

explanation.surface: A guess at what a garden watering can is.
explanation.definitionFit: To water crops or fields by channels or sprinklers is the job of this verb, which a watering can might be said to do.

definitions.meaning: to vet candidates is to check them over before approval
to broadcast a programme is to put it on air

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: vetting applicants means checking them, and a broadcaster airs a programme on the small display.

parts.note: a tag is a label or name, a title

explanation.surface: A second title of something is declared to be for men only.
explanation.walkthrough: A stag party or stag night is one for men only, before a wedding.
explanation.definitionFit: A stag event is an all-male gathering, hence the description men only.

clue.text: Blimey! The French right's more fashionable

parts.note: coo is an old British exclamation of surprise, like blimey
le is the French masculine word for the

explanation.surface: Surprise at the French political right being trendier.
explanation.walkthrough: COO and BLIMEY are both British exclamations of astonishment.
explanation.definitionFit: Cool is slang for stylish, so its comparative means trendier.

clue.text: Does my bum look big in this?

definitions.text: Does my bum look big in this?

parts.words: Does my bum look big in this?
parts.note: the classic anxious question about clothing, here asked of a Victorian hooped underskirt that made the rear vast on purpose

explanation.surface: The stock question someone asks while trying on clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: This stiff hooped petticoat held Victorian skirts out wide, so the wearer certainly looked big below the waist.

clue.text: Smooth Blair cut apart by English

indicators.note: apart signals the two words are broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: A former prime minister being taken to pieces by the English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'apart' rearranges BLAIR and CUT into LUBRICAT; 'by' places E beside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To oil machinery is to make its moving parts run without friction, a smoothing action.

indicators.note: carrying means the word for firm holds the abbreviation inside

parts.note: firm and hard both mean solid and unyielding

explanation.surface: A company holding outdated stock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Firm' looks like a business; it is the adjective HARD.
explanation.definitionFit: A stockpile or store of supplies is a hidden reserve.

indicators.note: in means the article and the politician go inside the word for a retreat

parts.note: a den is a private retreat or study
MP stands for Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A politician hiding away is feeble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wet' looks like the British sense of a weak politician, but it is the verb meaning to moisten.
explanation.definitionFit: To moisten something slightly is to make it damp, i.e. wet it.

indicators.note: In tells us the letters sit within the run of words slander I detect

explanation.surface: Someone spotting an insult concealed within slander.
explanation.definitionFit: To mock or ridicule is to treat with contempt, an insulting act.

clue.text: Fish on grand stream for fish

parts.note: G is slang for a grand, a thousand pounds or dollars
a ray is a beam or stream of light
the ling is a long-bodied sea fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: Angling on a great river for fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stream' suggests a river, but it is a stream of light, a RAY.
explanation.definitionFit: The grayling is a freshwater game fish of the salmon family.

indicators.note: say signals that the word for strip is pronounced, giving a different spelling

parts.note: a band is a strip of material

explanation.surface: Asking whether a strip show was censored.
explanation.definitionFit: Censored material is prohibited, forbidden from publication.

clue.text: Fall down dead with bad back

indicators.note: back signals that the word for bad is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: poor quality means bad quality

explanation.surface: Someone with a bad back collapsing as if dead.
explanation.definitionFit: To sag or hang limply is to sink downwards, falling slowly.

clue.text: Moderately left in labour, for example

indicators.note: in means the abbreviation for left sits inside the word for a political group

parts.note: Labour is an example of a political party

explanation.surface: A woman described as somewhat left alone while giving birth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'labour' suggests childbirth; it stands for the British Labour Party.
explanation.definitionFit: Partly means to some extent, in part, which is to a moderate degree.

indicators.note: terribly signals the letters are badly jumbled
endlessly signals the final letter of seems is dropped

explanation.surface: A former prime minister appears awfully unhappy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts SEEMS to SEEM; 'terribly' then rearranges BLAIR with SEEM.
explanation.definitionFit: Wretched and unhappy in the extreme are synonyms describing deep misery.

clue.text: Ceremony is just for the audience

indicators.note: for the audience signals a word as heard by listeners, spelt another way

parts.note: just and right both mean fair and proper

explanation.surface: A ceremony justified as being only for spectators.
explanation.definitionFit: A rite is a formal religious or solemn ritual.

parts.note: ado is fuss or commotion
RN is the Royal Navy, a body of sailors

explanation.surface: A disturbance among sailors on a ship's deck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deck' suggests a ship's floor; it is the verb meaning to decorate.
explanation.definitionFit: To deck a room is to decorate or embellish it.

parts.note: F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine
fine weather is fair weather

explanation.surface: Praise of a lovely love story.
explanation.definitionFit: A romantic liaison, often secret, is a love relationship.

parts.note: Desperate Dan is a strongman in the British children's comic The Dandy
the heart of the word sweet is its middle letter E

explanation.surface: A hopeless figure courting a loved one, like the tragic prince.
explanation.walkthrough: Hamlet is the Prince of Denmark; the question mark marks him as an example of a Scandinavian.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's prince is from Denmark, so he is a native of that country.

indicators.note: turning signals the letters are rotated round into a new order

explanation.surface: An argument degenerating into chaos.
explanation.definitionFit: Diabetes is a metabolic medical condition, a disorder of blood sugar.

parts.note: to belie is to contradict or give the lie to

explanation.surface: Disputing so-called women's intuition.
explanation.definitionFit: An intuition is a feeling or conviction held without proof, a kind of faith.

clue.text: Voice of no. Ten, I fancy

indicators.note: fancy as an adjective means elaborate, signalling the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Someone imagining they are the voice of Downing Street.
explanation.walkthrough: No. 10 Downing Street is the British prime minister's residence.
explanation.definitionFit: To intone is to utter or chant in a level tone, to voice words.

indicators.note: not signals the letter for posh is removed from the word for fashionable

parts.note: popular means in fashion
U means upper-class, the posh style

explanation.surface: A tree described as trendy but not upper-class.
explanation.walkthrough: U as upper-class comes from 1950s British talk of 'U and non-U' usage.
explanation.definitionFit: Aspen is a species of the same genus, Populus, a kind of tree.

clue.text: Bush, perhaps admitting Iran's first yielding

indicators.note: admitting means letting the letter into the middle of the word for a shrub

parts.note: a bush is an example of a plant

indicators.note: first takes the opening letter of Iran's

explanation.surface: President Bush letting Iran in first and appearing to give way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bush' suggests the US president; it is a shrub.
explanation.definitionFit: Pliant and yielding both mean flexible and easily bent.

parts.note: Tiger Woods' assistant carrying his golf clubs, the woods, around the course

explanation.surface: A forester carrying timber.
explanation.definitionFit: A golfer's attendant carries the bag of clubs, including the wooden-headed drivers.

parts.note: pa is a word for father, plus the possessive s
to try food is to taste it

explanation.surface: A father's samplings of tarts.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarts are baked items of pastry, a kind of sweet bakery goods.

indicators.note: initially takes the opening letters of Silky, and, radiant and Indian

explanation.surface: A description of a shining silk Indian garment.
explanation.definitionFit: The whole clue describes the shimmering draped garment worn by Indian women.

clue.text: One's on top of the world!

definitions.text: One's on top of the world!

parts.words: One's on top of the world!
parts.note: sounds like a person elated, but describes the frozen cap at the Earth's poles

explanation.surface: A cry of joy from someone feeling elated.
explanation.definitionFit: A polar sheet of permanent ice sits at the top of the globe.

indicators.note: about means the word for row surrounds the letter

parts.note: a bank is a row, as of keys or switches

indicators.note: leader takes the opening letter of labour

explanation.surface: A mindless argument about a Labour leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' looks like an argument; it is a line, a BANK.
explanation.definitionFit: A blank expression is empty and vacant, without thought.

clue.text: Agreed on a cocktail for drink

indicators.note: a cocktail is a mixture, signalling the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: Settling on a cocktail as the drink to have.
explanation.definitionFit: A fizzy citrus soft drink is a beverage.
